title: First Position in a Sorted List
description:
A list of integers is sorted in non-decreasing order and may contain repeated values. Given a query value x, print the smallest index (0-based) at which x appears, or -1 if x does not appear.

Input format
Line 1: n, the length of the list.
Line 2: the n integers.
Line 3: the query value x.

Output format
One integer: the first index of x, or -1.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000. The list is sorted in non-decreasing order. Values are between -1000000000 and 1000000000. A solution that scans the whole list will be too slow on the largest tests; aim for O(log n).
hints: Finding any occurrence is binary search. The twist is that you must find the leftmost one.
When the middle value equals x, you cannot stop: there may be more copies to the left. Keep searching the left half while remembering this index as a candidate.
Use lo = 0, hi = n - 1, ans = -1. If a[mid] >= x move hi = mid - 1 (and if a[mid] == x set ans = mid); otherwise lo = mid + 1. Return ans.

examples.explanation: The value 2 appears at indices 1, 2 and 3; the first is 1.
